dossier.purpose: Content-only repository of agent 'skills' (Markdown SKILL.md procedures) by Matt Pocock. 35 skills in five buckets: 18 engineering + 7 productivity (the 'promoted' set of 25, shipped as a Claude Code plugin) plus 6 beta 'in-progress' and 4 'misc' skills that are installable only through the external skills.sh installer (skills/in-progress/README.md:3-9; CHANGELOG.md:132). Topics: grilling interviews, specs and tickets, TDD, bug diagnosis, code review, domain modelling, architecture surveys, merge-conflict resolution, research, prototyping. 11 promoted skills are model-invoked (description-triggered); 14 are user-invoked only. Codex support is per-skill agents/openai.yaml metadata installed via skills.sh; there is no native Codex plugin. No dedicated security-review, threat-model or vulnerability procedure exists in the tree; security-adjacent content is limited to redaction notes, the wizard's hidden secret entry, and an unpromoted Claude-Code-only git-guardrails hook. No runtime service, CLI, MCP server or SDK. File counts below were obtained with Glob/Grep/Read only (shell was unavailable).

claims.claim: 'My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding.'
'These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model.'

Two install routes with different philosophies: the Claude Code plugin 'installs the whole set as a managed, read-only bundle that updates when I ship'; skills.sh 'copies editable skill files into your project'. 'Pick one — installing both leaves you with every skill twice.'
`claude plugins install mattpocock-skills` (or `/plugin install mattpocock-skills`). 'It's in Claude Code's official marketplace, so there's nothing to add first, and updates arrive automatically.'
Codex and other agents: `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills`; 'Pick the skills you want, and which coding agents to install them on'; make sure `setup-matt-pocock-skills` is one of them.
'A native Codex plugin is on the roadmap' (points to ADR 0002).
skills.sh 'writes the skills into your repo as ordinary files you own and can edit. Nothing updates behind your back'; pull updates with `npx skills update`.
Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` once per repo: it asks which issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, or local files), which triage labels, and where docs are saved.
Skills exist to fix failure modes 'with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents'.

User-invoked skills 'are reachable only when you type them'; model-invoked skills 'can be invoked by you or reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits'. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, never another user-invoked one.

Model-invoked set — Engineering: prototype, diagnosing-bugs, research, tdd, domain-modeling, codebase-design, code-review, resolving-merge-conflicts, wizard. Productivity: grilling, writing-for-agents. All other promoted skills are user-invoked.
`/tdd` 'encourages red-green-refactor'; `/diagnosing-bugs` 'wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase'.
`code-review`: two-axis review (Standards and Spec) 'run as parallel sub-agents so neither pollutes the other'.

install.method: skills.sh installer (Codex and other agents; also usable for Claude Code)
skills.sh, one skill only (documented in the internal install block and the in-progress README, not the top-level README)

install.command: npx skills update   (single skill: npx skills@latest update <name>)

install.command: /plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills  then  /plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home code exists in the repository (repo-wide search for telemetry/analytics terms found only unrelated prose; the tree has no runtime code beyond maintainer scripts and skill templates). README and docs state no telemetry policy either way, and the behaviour of the external `skills` installer (fetched at @latest, README.md:52) is not documented here. No account is needed for the skills themselves. Network and accounts arise from surrounding tools and specific skills: (1) Install — the official-marketplace listing points at the repo's git URL with a pinned sha (.agents/adr/0002-ship-as-a-claude-code-plugin.md:34,40); skills.sh fetches from GitHub. (2) Runtime — tracker skills (to-spec, to-tickets, triage, wayfinder, code-review's spec lookup) call the gh/glab CLIs against GitHub/GitLab and need an authenticated CLI (skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md:44-45; issue-tracker-github.md:3-45); `research` reads external primary sources through a background agent (skills/engineering/research/SKILL.md:10); improve-codebase-architecture's HTML report loads Tailwind (https://cdn.tailwindcss.com) and Mermaid (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/...) from CDNs when opened (HTML-REPORT.md:13-16, 100; docs/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture.md:60 says it breaks offline); wizard scripts open vendor dashboards and may run `gh secret set` (wizard/template.sh:65-75, 141-167). (3) README furniture only: images on res.cloudinary.com, a skills.sh badge and an aihero.dev newsletter link (README.md:2-13, 21-23).

entry_points.what: Claude Code plugin manifest (name mattpocock-skills, v1.2.3, MIT); explicit `skills` array of 25 promoted skill directories (lines 21-47); no hooks, MCP or commands fields.

code.architecture: Content-only repo with no executable runtime. skills/ has five buckets (CLAUDE.md:1-7): engineering/ (18 skills) and productivity/ (7) are 'promoted' and mirrored one-to-one by the explicit `skills` array in .claude-plugin/plugin.json (lines 21-47), the top-level README and a docs page each (docs/<bucket>/<skill>.md, 25 pages); misc/ (4), in-progress/ (6, all user-invoked) and deprecated/ (empty) are installable only via skills.sh. Each skill is a folder: SKILL.md (promoted bodies run from about 7 to about 140 lines), agents/openai.yaml, and optional reference files disclosed by pointer rather than inlined (e.g. tdd/tests.md + mocking.md, codebase-design/DEEPENING.md + DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md, domain-modeling/ADR-FORMAT.md + CONTEXT-FORMAT.md, prototype/LOGIC.md + UI.md, ask-matt/PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md, triage/AGENT-BRIEF.md + OUT-OF-SCOPE.md) and templates/scripts (wizard/template.sh, diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh, misc/git-guardrails-claude-code/scripts/block-dangerous-git.sh). Invocation model: 11 promoted skills are model-invoked, with descriptions that stay loaded by design (skills/productivity/writing-for-agents/SKILL-MECHANICS.md:9); 14 are user-invoked only, with no model reach (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:10; .agents/invocation.md:5-10). Skills depend on one another through `/skill` prose invocation (.agents/invocation.md:16): implement→tdd,code-review (implement/SKILL.md:9-13); tdd→codebase-design (tdd/SKILL.md:26); grill-with-docs→grilling,domain-modeling; triage and improve-codebase-architecture→grilling,domain-modeling; wayfinder→research,grilling,domain-modeling; to-spec, to-tickets, triage, wayfinder and code-review→setup-matt-pocock-skills, which writes per-repo docs/agents/* config (issue tracker via gh/glab or local .scratch/ markdown). Self-contained model-invoked skills: research, resolving-merge-conflicts (CHANGELOG.md:264), grilling, wizard, prototype. Supporting material: .agents/ (ADRs, install-block.md, invocation.md, writing-docs.md), .out-of-scope/ (3 rejected-request notes), .changeset/ and scripts/ (release plumbing).
code.packaging_and_release: No build step or distributable artifact; the repo itself is the artifact. Release is changesets-driven: .github/workflows/release.yml (on push to main, lines 3-6) runs checkout@v4, setup-node@v4 (Node 22), `npm ci`, then changesets/action@v1 with `version: npm run version` (changeset version + scripts/sync-plugin-version.mjs, package.json:13) and `publish: npx changeset tag` (release.yml:30-35), producing a 'chore: version skills' PR and git tags (annotated tag v1.2.3 peeling to 6acc160e…, .git/packed-refs:2-3). package.json is private (line 4), so nothing is published to npm; .changeset/config.json sets privatePackages version/tag true. No checksums, signatures, SBOM or provenance attestations appear in the workflow, and actions are pinned to major tags, not SHAs (release.yml:19, 22, 30). Distribution channels: the Claude Code official-marketplace listing, which pins a git sha and reads .claude-plugin/plugin.json (ADR 0002:34, 40), and skills.sh copying skill folders from GitHub. plugin.json (version 1.2.3, line 3) is kept equal to package.json (1.2.3, line 3) by the sync script.
code.tests_and_ci: No automated tests: no test files, test directories or test framework (globs for *.test.*, *.spec.* and test/tests/__tests__ directories returned nothing; approximate test-file count 0). CI is a single workflow, .github/workflows/release.yml (versioning only; no lint, validate or test job). Maintainer checks are manual: `claude plugin validate . --strict` after touching manifests (CLAUDE.md:11) and `npm run check-plugin-version` (package.json:14), which no workflow invokes. Repo invariants (every promoted skill in README + plugin.json, a docs page per skill, invocation flags paired with openai.yaml) are enforced by convention only (CLAUDE.md:9-21; .agents/invocation.md:10).
code.dependencies: One manifest: package.json — 0 runtime dependencies and 2 devDependencies (@changesets/cli ^2.30.0, @changesets/changelog-github ^0.7.0; package.json:16-19), private package, packageManager npm@10.9.4 (line 20). package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) has 111 node_modules entries (transitive, dev-only); its header still says version 0.0.0 (lines 3, 9). No other manifests (no requirements, go.mod, Cargo.toml, etc.). Tools that skills assume at use time but do not declare anywhere: gh and glab (tracker templates), jq (GitHub template and git-guardrails script), git, optional shellcheck (wizard/SKILL.md:41), the Claude Code CLI (`claude --bg` in in-progress/claude-handoff), and the Tailwind/Mermaid CDNs.
code.security_policy: none — no SECURITY.md (searched **/SECURITY*) and no .github/SECURITY.md; .github contains only workflows/release.yml. The only security-related note is a docs FAQ saying Snyk flags diagnosing-bugs as high risk, which the docs call a false positive (docs/engineering/diagnosing-bugs.md:73-74).

risks: Scope gap for security procedures: no skill covers threat modelling, vulnerability review, dependency audit or secure-coding checks. code-review's Standards axis is repo-documented standards plus 12 Fowler smells and 'skip anything tooling enforces' (skills/engineering/code-review/SKILL.md:34-56). Security-flavoured content is limited to diagnosing-bugs' Redact section (SKILL.md:12-16), handoff's redaction line (skills/productivity/handoff/SKILL.md:14), wizard's hidden secret entry (wizard/template.sh:113-126) and misc/git-guardrails-claude-code, which is Claude-Code-only, outside the plugin, substring-matching, and by inspection exits 0 (allows the command) if jq is missing because it has no jq check or set -e (scripts/block-dangerous-git.sh:3-25).

Catalog granularity: the plugin install is all-or-nothing (25 skills, .claude-plugin/plugin.json:21-47). By the repo's own design the 11 model-invoked skills keep always-loaded descriptions (skills/productivity/writing-for-agents/SKILL-MECHANICS.md:9) while the 14 user-invoked ones are outside model reach (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:10). Per-skill selection exists only via the external skills.sh installer (README.md:55; .agents/install-block.md:44), and skills depend on each other through /skill prose (implement→tdd,code-review: implement/SKILL.md:9-13; tdd→codebase-design: tdd/SKILL.md:26; grill-with-docs→grilling,domain-modeling: grill-with-docs/SKILL.md:7; five skills→setup-matt-pocock-skills), so a single-skill install can leave dangling references (CHANGELOG.md:231, 241; docs/engineering/tdd.md:25).

Claude Code vs Codex parity is partial and recorded as such: no native Codex plugin (README.md:57; ADR 0002:13-23); Codex once hid a skill from the model-visible list because of policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false (CHANGELOG.md:23); the setup skill picks CLAUDE.md over AGENTS.md regardless of harness (skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md:74-80; docs/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills.md:63); docs report Claude desktop/web omit user-invoked skills from the model's list (docs/engineering/ask-matt.md:56; docs/engineering/wizard.md:77) and that the plugin's mattpocock-skills: prefix makes Claude Code's built-in /code-review hard to reach (docs/engineering/code-review.md:52).

Sub-agent skills carry no recursion guard: code-review (SKILL.md:58-72) and research (SKILL.md:6) tell the agent to spawn sub-agents without forbidding re-invocation; project docs report 50-plus agents and about 450k tokens in single runs (docs/engineering/code-review.md:56; docs/engineering/research.md:35).

Maintenance and QA: no tests and no validation CI — the only workflow is versioning (.github/workflows/release.yml); manifest and sync checks are manual (CLAUDE.md:11; package.json:14). Docs drift against code is already visible at this tag: docs/engineering/diagnosing-bugs.md:71 says redaction is unimplemented vs SKILL.md:12-16; docs/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture.md:84 says the skill names Claude Code's Agent tool vs SKILL.md:27 and CHANGELOG.md:13; docs/engineering/wizard.md:44 still advertises time remaining vs CHANGELOG.md:15 and the template; docs/engineering/ask-matt.md:56 counts 13 of 22 vs 14 of 25 in code. Docs also list open, unfixed defects (e.g. docs/engineering/to-tickets.md:65-68; docs/engineering/triage.md:74).

Release and supply chain: no release artifacts, checksums, signatures or provenance; actions pinned to major tags not SHAs (release.yml:19, 22, 30). Plugin users receive changes only when the official listing's pinned sha moves — it lagged two commits behind main when last verified (ADR 0002:40). `npx skills@latest` runs an unpinned external package at install time (README.md:52; .agents/install-block.md:53) whose behaviour, including any telemetry, is not documented in this repo.

Runtime side effects and network: improve-codebase-architecture writes an HTML report that loads Tailwind and Mermaid (major-pinned only) from CDNs with Mermaid securityLevel 'loose' (HTML-REPORT.md:13-16) and fails offline (docs/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture.md:60); wizard templates write secrets to a plaintext .env and run gh secret set, with no .gitignore handling anywhere in the wizard files (template.sh:128-154); implement commits to the current branch (implement/SKILL.md:15); triage, to-spec, to-tickets and wayfinder create, label, comment on and close GitHub/GitLab issues via gh/glab (setup-matt-pocock-skills/issue-tracker-github.md:7-45; triage/SKILL.md:13-17). These tracker skills are user-invoked only; wizard is model-invoked but its script is not run by the agent (wizard/SKILL.md:43).

Maintainership: all 41 CHANGELOG entries credit one GitHub user (CHANGELOG.md:7-270), LICENSE is MIT with a single copyright holder (LICENSE:3), and there is no CODEOWNERS, CONTRIBUTING or SECURITY file. The project lists scope it will not take (.out-of-scope/mainstream-issue-trackers-only.md; question-limits.md; setup-skill-verify-mode.md), states edits to scripts/link-skills.sh won't be approved (lines 4-6), and its docs say plugin copies are read-only and skills.sh copies are overwritten on update, so durable local customisation means forking (docs/engineering/ask-matt.md:72; docs/engineering/code-review.md:52).
